document.title: VMware vSphere Automation REST API Programming Guide 8.0

capability_sources.note: Endpoint path and every field name used (host, name, connection_state, power_state) confirmed directly from VMware's own generated Python client source (com.vmware.vcenter_client.Host.Summary/FilterSpec), not vendor prose alone. ConnectionState (CONNECTED, DISCONNECTED, NOT_RESPONDING) and PowerState (POWERED_ON, POWERED_OFF, STANDBY) enum members were read from the same source file. The response is a JSON array at the top level, confirmed via the official Ansible vmware.vmware_rest collection's documented vcenter_host_info module output shape, which is generated from the same real API.
Endpoint path and field names (cluster, name, ha_enabled, drs_enabled) confirmed directly from the same generated Python client source (com.vmware.vcenter_client.Cluster.Summary/FilterSpec).

VM.Summary's field set (vm, name, power_state, cpu_count, memory_size_MiB) could not be located in VMware's own generated Python client source directly (the vcenter_client.py module excerpt available did not include the VM class body), so it was independently confirmed via the official Ansible vmware.vmware_rest collection's vcenter_vm_info module documentation -- generated from the same real vSphere Automation API OpenAPI definitions -- which documents this exact field set including a literal example response. PowerState enum members (POWERED_OFF, POWERED_ON, SUSPENDED) were separately confirmed from the real com.vmware.vcenter.vm_client.Power.State source.

authentication_source.note: Confirmed via Broadcom's own official TechDocs page, which shows a real, working curl example: 'curl -k -i -X POST -H "Authorization: Basic $auth" https://$VC/api/session' followed by extracting the session id from the vmware-api-session-id response HEADER (not the response body) via 'awk "/vmware-api-session-id/ {print $2}"' against curl's -i header output. This is a real, deliberate difference from every other connector built for this project so far (Hitachi, Brocade, both Huawei products), which all return their session/auth token in a JSON response body. DELETE /api/session with the same header logs out; this connector follows the established login -> read -> logout bounded-cycle pattern used for both Huawei connectors, never caching a live session.

self_test_source.note: No confirmed dedicated version/compatibility endpoint independent of the inventory reads was found; the self-test reuses the host-inventory read itself, the same pattern used for Brocade SANnav and both Huawei connectors.

unconfirmed_gaps: No confirmed field on any list response (host, cluster, or vm summary) carries a parent-cluster or running-host identifier -- FilterSpec accepts clusters/hosts as query filters, but resolving membership would require per-entity filtered calls this first pass does not make. Host-to-cluster and VM-to-host graph relationships are therefore not represented; this is stated plainly in the graph adapter's known_gaps rather than fabricated.

Datastore, network, and resource-pool inventory (/api/vcenter/datastore, /api/vcenter/network, /api/vcenter/resource-pool) are real, confirmed vSphere Automation API endpoints that were not implemented in this first pass -- only host, cluster, and VM inventory.
